tweet_summary: German-language tweet by Georg Pazderski claiming Kyiv took 3rd place in Europe for Bentley sales in 2025 (behind Padua and Rotterdam), implying war-time Ukraine luxury sales are booming and using this to question EU aid. The tweet implies high sales volumes ('mostly high-end models 400-450k$').
why_note_decision: Per multiple sources (Bentley Kyiv's own LinkedIn post, EADaily, MythDetector, autonext.co, the user @ITUADE in replies), the '3rd place' is Bentley's internal Business Performance Matrix / European Scorecard Awards 2025 ranking, which evaluates 61 dealerships on 12 KPIs (sales, marketing, operational excellence, customer experience, etc.) — NOT a sales-volume ranking. Actual 2025 Bentley sales in Ukraine were ~20 cars. The tweet's clear implication — that Ukraine sold more Bentleys than nearly any other European city while at war — is misleading; the dealership ranked well on combined operational KPIs, not on sales numbers. CN is warranted. The original note IS correct and cites both the LinkedIn original and EADaily. Failure mode: raters tagged 'missing key points' (4) and 'note not needed' (4) on only 94 ratings; probably the note's brevity / lack of explicit '20 cars sold' framing kept it from cleanly winning, plus political polarization in replies.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note (a) clarifies that '3rd place' refers to Bentley's internal European Scorecard / Business Performance Matrix evaluating dealerships across ~12 KPIs (sales, marketing, customer experience, operational excellence), NOT sales volume, (b) provides the actual 2025 Bentley registration figure in Ukraine (~20 cars), and (c) cites at least one reputable source (Bentley Kyiv's LinkedIn post, AFP fact-check, MythDetector, EADaily, or autonext.co). FAIL the note if it (a) merely says 'this is misleading' without explaining the KPI vs. sales distinction, (b) cites only the LinkedIn dealership post without the sales-volume context, or (c) doesn't refute the headline framing that Ukraine is selling Bentleys at scale. The original note covers (a), (b) approximately ('20 Bentleys verkauft'), and (c) — it is acceptable but on the lean side; a stronger note also references the AFP fact-check.

importance.lens_rationale: Russian-aligned narrative pushing 'Ukraine aid funds luxury cars' to undermine EU support for Ukraine in a live war — correcting this matters for the broader information environment around the war.
